clue.text: Views unlimited gear

indicators.note: without limits, so the word for views loses its first and last letters

parts.note: views are opinions, someone's held beliefs

explanation.surface: A boast about equipment that offers views without limit, like a camera or telescope mount.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinion is a small cogwheel that meshes with a larger wheel or rack, a piece of gearing.

clue.text: Not getting going, failing to start drunken tirade

indicators.note: drunken means staggering about, so the remaining letters of going are jumbled
the word going fails at its start, so it loses its first letter

parts.note: a tirade is a rant, an angry outburst

explanation.surface: Someone too drunk to get their angry speech off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not getting' is the definition, in the slang sense of failing to understand; 'drunken' scrambles the shortened word made by 'failing to start'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ignorant does not understand or know, so is not getting it in the colloquial sense.

clue.text: One trapped in sadness pattern, turning to these

definitions.text: One trapped in sadness pattern, turning to these

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside, so the letter for one sits within the other letters
turning means the letters of sadness and pattern are twisted into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a cycle of low mood seeks help from medication.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a person caught in a pattern of sadness might turn to these pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Antidepressants are medicines prescribed for depression, which a person trapped in persistent sadness might be given.

clue.text: Stored unfinished piece of work in hut

indicators.note: in means the shortened work goes inside the word for hut

parts.note: a shed is a simple hut

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for a piece of work loses its last letter

parts.note: a task is a piece of work to be done

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a half-done job tucked away in their garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash something is to store it away, usually hidden for later use.

clue.text: Those on the way out frequently go through it

definitions.text: Those on the way out frequently go through it

parts.words: Those on the way out frequently go through it
parts.note: sounds like the dying, but it describes travellers leaving by air, who pass through the waiting area at an airport

explanation.surface: A grim remark about the dying passing through some final stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way out' suggests death; here it simply means flying out of an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: At an airport, passengers about to fly off wait in this hall before boarding their flights.

clue.text: Shivering with cold, I get hot dish

parts.note: a chill is a feverish cold with shivering

explanation.surface: Someone frozen through is served something spicy to warm up.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli, short for chilli con carne, is a spicy meat stew, a dish full of heat.

clue.text: Knocking back slightly raised drink

indicators.note: in this down answer the back letter of the knocking word is lifted a little higher up the column

parts.note: pinking is the knocking sound of an engine misfiring

explanation.surface: Someone downing a drink and feeling a little lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: PINKING's last letter G moves up two places to give PINKGIN; in a down clue 'raised' means moved up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink gin is gin flavoured with Angostura bitters, a traditional naval cocktail.

clue.text: Section madman, one that can easily be turned loose

definitions.text: one that can easily be turned loose

parts.note: a wing is a section of a building or organisation
a nut is slang for a madman

explanation.surface: A lunatic in the asylum's ward who could easily be set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned loose' suggests releasing a captive; it means unscrewed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing nut has two flat projections so it can be undone by finger and thumb without a spanner.

clue.text: See 8
Foreign assembly of European heads in The Hague, nothing in common

indicators.note: heads are the first letters, here of each word from European to common, with assembly of telling us to collect them

explanation.surface: European leaders gather at The Hague but find no common ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic can describe something from another culture, as in ethnic food, so it serves loosely for foreign.

clue.text: I see endless life around an Italian town

indicators.note: around means the whole string is turned to read the other way

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

indicators.note: endless means the word for life drops its final letter

parts.note: vita is Latin for life

explanation.surface: A mystic claiming to see a past life lived in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns I + LO + VIT round to give the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tivoli is a hill town near Rome, famous for the Villa d'Este and Hadrian's Villa.

clue.text: Brilliant old general introduced line similar to Polaris

indicators.note: introduced means the line letter is brought in between the other pieces

parts.note: star as an adjective means brilliant or outstanding
Ike was the nickname of General Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A dazzling general from the past brings in a policy line resembling a missile programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Polaris suggests the submarine missile, but it is the Pole Star.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris is the Pole Star, so something resembling it is like a star.

clue.text: Signs of future union battle with self-interest groups

parts.note: an engagement is a battle between forces
rings are cliques or cartels working together for their own gain

explanation.surface: Omens of a trade union merger amid infighting between cliques.
explanation.definitionFit: These are worn by people betrothed to marry, a sign of the wedding to come.

clue.text: See 7
One male deserting in army uniform

parts.note: a unit is one, a single thing

indicators.note: deserting means the male letter leaves the word army

parts.note: taken as the word army

explanation.surface: A lone soldier going absent without leave while still in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army uniform' reads as one phrase, but 'uniform' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unitary means single and undivided, so consistent and uniform throughout.

clue.text: Celestial event with peak on Mars having oxygen gas enshrouding it

indicators.note: enshrouding means the gas wraps around the other letters

parts.note: neon is a noble gas

indicators.note: the peak of a word in a down clue is its top, first letter

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An astronomer describes a mountain on Mars wrapped in an oxygen atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lunar phase when the dark side faces Earth, an event in the sky's monthly cycle.

clue.text: Deliver gift here

definitions.meaning: to deliver a speech or award is to give it formally
here means in attendance, as when answering a roll call

explanation.surface: A courier's instruction to drop the parcel off at this address.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to hand over formally, a gift, and in attendance: three unrelated senses.

clue.text: On which one may log which people will crack short grey-wether

indicators.note: crack means break open, so the pronoun goes inside the shortened stone
short means the stone's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a grey-wether is a sarsen, a large sandstone boulder found on English downland
who is the pronoun for which people

explanation.surface: A puzzling scene of people splitting a weathered stone on a log.
explanation.walkthrough: 'log' here is a verb, to cut timber into logs, not to record something.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawhorse is a frame that holds timber steady while it is cut with a saw.

clue.text: Pursuit of what's done by current setter

parts.note: the past is what is over and done
I is the symbol for electric current
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler describing their hobby and what they currently get up to.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is a hobby or recreational activity, something one pursues for pleasure.

clue.text: Fringe acts start to steal lyrics — they do indulge themselves

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lyrics are the words of a song
wallowers are people who indulge themselves, as in self-pity

explanation.surface: A festival performer pinching song lyrics while others revel in excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringe' suggests a festival fringe, but it means street-show or sideshow acts.
explanation.definitionFit: These are circus and sideshow performers who appear to swallow blades, novelty acts on the margins of entertainment.

clue.text: Game run by thief when cover has been blown

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: the cover of a down word is its top, so the thief loses its first letter

parts.note: a mugger is a street thief

explanation.surface: An undercover thief exposed during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugger is British slang for rugby union, a team sport.

clue.text: They may charge you old money (shillings)

parts.note: rhino is old British slang for money
S is the abbreviation for shillings, the old British coin worth twelve pence

explanation.surface: A complaint about being charged in pre-decimal currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge you' suggests billing, but it means a rampaging attack by the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoceroses are known for rushing headlong at intruders, so they may charge at a person.

clue.text: One who leaves record company funding from the public

parts.note: EMI is a British record label
a grant is money given from public funds

explanation.surface: A musician quitting a label that relies on public subsidy.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant is a person who leaves their own country to settle in another.

clue.text: See 16
Perfect state of excellent dope you mentioned, passing it round

indicators.note: passing a joint round suggests turning, so the words for excellent and dope are read the other way

parts.note: A1, written AI, means excellent
pot is slang for cannabis, dope

indicators.note: mentioned means said aloud, giving the letter that sounds like the word you

parts.note: the word you is spoken here

explanation.surface: A stoner's idea of paradise: great weed handed round the circle.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 for excellent is written with the letter I standing for the figure 1; 'passing it round', like a joint, signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia, from Thomas More's book, is an imagined ideal society, a flawless state.

clue.text: Powerful businessman?

definitions.meaning: powerful as in a convincing, forceful argument
read as company gent, CO being company and gent a man, so a man of business; the question mark flags the wordplay

explanation.surface: A one-word question asking whether a mighty figure is a tycoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is forceful and convincing, so powerful in persuasion.

clue.text: Snap warning that a cuppa might scald?

definitions.meaning: a snap is a photograph, here one taken by police

definitions.text: warning that a cuppa might scald?
definitions.meaning: split as ..., a warning that the tea's cup is too hot to touch

explanation.surface: A sharp warning at tea time that the drink is too hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug shot is a police photograph of a suspect's face, a kind of snapshot.
